topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture Series and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the scope of the cancer lecture course, and the learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: The Nature of Cancer and Interacting Mutation Drivers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by a combination of endogenous cellular processes, genetic predispositions, and external exposures.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures, Public Perception, and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures correlate with cancer incidence across populations and how the public interprets cancer causation versus chance.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, illustrated in detail by the discovery and mechanism of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Molecular Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how specific dietary, environmental, and chemical agents undergo metabolic processing to cause DNA adducts, transversions, and cellular damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammatory Microenvironments, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis including tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, tissue microenvironments, and developmental windows of vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity and Risk Evaluation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the experimental assays, genomic mutational signatures, and epidemiological models used to prove carcinogenicity and balance human risk.
